title: Light entering glass at 40°
caption: Entering glass (n = 1.52) at 40° the ray bends towards the normal: sin θ₂ = sin 40°/1.52 = 0.423, so θ₂ = 25°. Light rays are reversible: the same ray leaving the glass at 25° emerges into air at 40°. A weak reflected ray (about 4% at normal incidence) leaves at 40° too.
alt: Two ray diagrams: a ray in air at 40° entering glass bends towards the normal to 25°; a ray in glass at 25° leaves into air at 40°.
description: A ray in air strikes a glass surface (n = 1.52) at 40° to the normal. A faint reflected ray leaves at 40° on the other side of the normal.
Snell's law: sin θ₂ = sin 40°/1.52 = 0.423, so θ₂ = 25°: the refracted ray bends towards the normal in the denser glass.
Second panel: the reverse path. A ray in glass meeting the surface at 25° leaves into air at 40°, away from the normal.
